statement: The best open-weight model reaches the frontier score of 6 months earlier (Epoch Capabilities Index; rolling, 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Condition not holding (lag > 6 months), med confidence. The Epoch Capabilities Index did not exist. Best open-weight models (176B open-access multilingual model, July 2022; 130B bilingual model, Oct 2022) claimed parity with or modest gains over the 2020 frontier model (GPT-3 175B), while the closed frontier by mid-2022 (540B-parameter model, April 2022, state-of-the-art few-shot on hundreds of benchmarks) was well ahead - implying a lag of roughly 1.5-2 years on available comparisons.

items.summary: A Bloc B lab's open 130B model claimed significant outperformance over the 2020 frontier model (GPT-3 175B) on many English benchmarks, and noted that two other 175B-scale open models did not show that advantage - i.e. best open models were near the 2020 frontier.
items.detail: GLM-130B, arXiv:2210.02414 (verified via web_extract this run; abstract text is v2 2023-10-25, v1 2022-10-05).

items.summary: A 176B-parameter open-access multilingual model (46 languages, 13 programming languages) was released under a responsible-AI licence, trained on a public supercomputer funded by a non-top-3 government.
items.detail: BigScience BLOOM model card on Hugging Face (verified via web_extract this run): version 1.3 dated 2022-07-06, release date estimate 2022-07-11, RAIL License v1.0, Jean Zay supercomputer, 384 A100 GPUs. Paper arXiv:2211.05100 (Nov 2022) also opened, body not read.

items.summary: Closed frontier reference ~8 months before the window: a Bloc A developer's 540B model reported state-of-the-art few-shot results on hundreds of benchmarks and outperformed average human performance on a large benchmark suite.
items.detail: PaLM, arXiv:2204.02311 (verified via web_extract this run).

items.summary: No capabilities index comparable to the indicator's source existed; the first broad standardised benchmark of 30 language models spanning open, limited-access and closed models was launched just before the window.
items.detail: Stanford CRFM, 'Language Models are Changing AI: The Need for Holistic Evaluation' (HELM), 2022-11-17 (verified via web_extract this run). Its open-vs-closed findings were not read from an as-of version and are not used.
